description: Fresh formal check of the explored same-instance decision discrepancy, with real executor-produced recovery admission and full ordered command-content comparison. The original decision at node0 is the reference; the later completed handler suffix at node3 is compared only if it commits.

harness.description: Controlled actual-handler schedule with codec receipt, per-type FIFO dispatch and a real recovery-trigger worker.
semantic_changes: Bound allocation to eight instances per row; omit autonomous peer listeners and protocol event loops, preserving their selected dispatch semantics.
Buffer sockets and explicitly separate receipt from per-type dispatch; model one peer crash using the Alive eligibility change.
Run the actual executor only at node3 for its known hole; use unbuffered recovery queue to suspend it at the next request and synchronize cleanup.
Emit command JSON and status snapshots; target code and message fields are not replaced.

legality.derivation: The fixed helper mirrors N=5,F=2 constructor defaults and buffers actual SendMsg bytes, with all messages decoded via the registered New/Unmarshal factory. collect performs peer receipt/decoding and creates receiver message-type queues; deliver asserts FIFO within each receiver/type before dispatching the actual handler. This preserves the layer implemented by S-receive and S-dispatch: different RPC types enter different channels, so pending Commit0 need not dispatch before later PreAccept1. Original row0.instance0 is fast-committed by actual replies from peers1/2, then delivered to peer2. One peer1 crash is represented by making Alive[1]=false at all live nodes and never scheduling it again; peer loss updates that eligibility in S-receive. No new peer order or messages are fabricated. Thrifty failover sends next row0.instance1 to peers2/3. Node3 receives it while old Commit0 remains queued, so crtInstance[0]=1 with missing slot0, checked before the actual executeCommands loop starts. All protocol states are quiescent during the timer loop. It emits the real instancesToRecover request after its own counter; the harness checks row/instance identity and dispatches startRecoveryForInstance as run does. The queue is unbuffered solely to suspend the executor on its next instance1 request. This is a scheduling refinement of the original buffered producer, which may be suspended at the same send point; it does not change which first request was produced or the protocol state. Between sends for instance0 and instance1 the executor only increments k and reads unchanged crtInstance; it cannot read/write instance state while the recovery handlers run. The fixed handler suffix obtains a quorum from peers2/4, then dispatches the emitted phase1 and Accept exchanges with peers4/0. All decisions derive from target handlers, not installed snapshots. At the fixed observation point node3 live state has no concurrent executor access. Cleanup sets Shutdown only after observation, receives the next instance1 request, then joins the executor; the unbuffered send/receive orders the Shutdown write before the next loop read. Cleanup is independent of the compared result. Pending Commit and other messages remain visible and no global quiescence or eventual progress is assumed.
legality.applicability: Static volatile N=5,F=2; one crash at peer1; node0 and node3 never fail during the comparison.

grounding.derivation: initial_decision is emitted after actual COMMITTED status at node0; commands is json.Marshal of the full ordered []state.Command, containing operation, key and value bytes. recovery_requested follows the actual executor request with an explicit first.status predecessor condition; the fixed later result is correlated by row/instance, not by command or ballot. At result, committed is actual Status>=COMMITTED and commands is the same complete encoding. The implication compares content only when the later participant commits. A false antecedent would mean no later commit in this schedule, not universal agreement. Sampling is under synchronous ownership with the executor suspended between requests.
grounding.applicability: One original instance, one actual recovery request, one fixed suffix result.

observable_properties.description: A later commitment for the same instance preserves the original ordered command batch.

uncertainties: No isolation of one necessary root cause among interacting recovery/formation mechanisms.
The schedule delays pending message types and suspends the executor at a reachable request boundary; production autonomous scheduling is not replayed wall-clock for wall-clock.
No client-visible/application endpoint or universal recovery result is inferred.
